Hi Alice — thanks for the forecast and the clear asks. High-level response below; I'll follow up with a one-page commercial that you can share with procurement.

1) Pooling: Yes — we can pool usage across teams under a single account-level commit. That means the 25M gen tokens + 25M embedding-equivalent would count toward the same committed tier for discounting.

2) Blended pricing approach: Because streaming (chat) and embeddings have different cost profiles, we typically use an equivalent-token conversion for embeddings and apply a blended discount schedule on total committed tokens. Example proposal (ballpark):
   - Tier A: 0-10M committed tokens/month — standard list price
   - Tier B: 10-50M committed tokens/month — 8% discount off list
   - Tier C: 50-200M committed tokens/month — 12% discount off list
   - Additional negotiated pricing for >200M

   For mixed workloads we apply a 1:1.0 conversion for gen tokens and 0.5 conversion for embedding items (so 5M embeddings -> counts as 2.5M for commit). We can tweak conversion factors if Acme prefers an embeddings-focused structure.

3) Pilot / ramp: We typically offer a ramp credit for the first 90 days to reduce deployment friction. For example: 50% credit on committed spend up to the first 20M tokens in month 1-3, then ramp to committed levels in months 4-6.

4) Roll-forward & overage: We can offer a quarterly roll-forward of unused commit for up to one quarter. Overage beyond committed tiers billed at list price with a 3% grace buffer on monthly overages; we include a 30-day notice for changes to committed bands.

Attachments: I'll put a formal pricing spreadsheet and a draft SOW after internal alignment (ETA tomorrow).
